While traditional methods like credit cards or loan applications typically treat gambling as a personal debt, payday loans offer a different kind of safety net for those who cannot afford to lose money. Payday loans are short-term, high-interest loans typically due on your next payday. Unlike credit cards that offer extended grace periods, payday loans have a short repayment window ranging from one to seven days. This means you might borrow just enough to cover immediate expenses, then repay the balance by your next paycheck. The interest rate is usually higher than traditional credit cards due to the speed of repayment.

For someone living on a tight budget, this can feel like a lifeline. However, they must be cautious about the terms. Banks often charge exorbitant fees for processing and origination charges, which can eat into any savings you might have.
